newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P sees stable NZ ratings outlook, some threats.
newsitem.headline: S&P sees stable NZ ratings outlook, some threats.

text.p: International credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it felt fundraising entities across all sectors of the New Zealand economy continued to display stable credit quality despite what it called increasingly difficult operating conditions.

In a special report on New Zealand, which has an AA+ long- term rating on its sovereign foreign debt and a AAA local currency debt rating, S&P called the credit quality of financial institutions "stable, but under some pressure".

"The banking system in New Zealand has reached a stage of maturity, where further gains in profitability will only be achieved from significant cost reductions and improved economies of scale," S&P wrote.
The agency said it anticipates some rationalisation in the number of industry participants, a view that is commonly shared among local market observers in the country.

On the insurance industry, S&P said it felt the credit quality outlook was stable in the medium term but it was aware that the industry was "unsettled in pricing, products, distribution and competition".
Its forward view for insurance reflected its belief that these pressures would ease in the short term "and conditions are within the tolerance of existing ratings".
